question: After resolving the conflict and functional blocker, should Execa become the canonical dependency for OpenClaw's core process-execution boundary?
rationale: This intentionally replaces high-blast-radius lifecycle and platform behavior while adding a substantial runtime dependency cone, so an owner must accept the architectural, compatibility, and supply-chain tradeoff.

options.title: Adopt after parity proof
options.body: Land the Execa layer after conflict resolution, stream-error repair, dependency audit, and representative Linux and Windows runtime proof.

options.title: Retain the current layer
options.body: Decline the dependency migration if its semantic or supply-chain cost outweighs the consolidation benefit.

recommendation.title: Adopt after parity proof
recommendation.body: Land the Execa layer after conflict resolution, stream-error repair, dependency audit, and representative Linux and Windows runtime proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied evidence identifies steipete as the design author and the contributor most directly connected to this execution-layer and dependency decision.
